LESSON: READING 13.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Savings Suggested vocabulary wealth, income, needs, wants, spend, cost, save, po
Topic 13.2: Reading 13.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.2.1 Fluency, part of Savings Suggested vocabulary wealth, income, needs, wants, spend, cost, save, po in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read at the right speed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 13.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is developed as they read a grade-appropriate text accurately, at the right speed and

with expressions,

• Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to interact with technology is improved as they participate in reading a text in readers’ theatre with peers and

record on a digital device with assistive technology.

Values:
Respect is cultivated as the learner appreciates the effort of peers as they engage in timed reading and give positive feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life-skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is boosted as they gain reading fluency skills.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses the reading fluency skills acquired when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
